title: They were still talking about him… but less.
paragraphs: They were still talking about him… but less.
You could feel it in the air.
The crowds hadn’t disappeared overnight. The river still moved. The dust still lifted under sandals. But something shifted. The voices that once shouted his name now whispered another.
And he heard it.
“They’re all going to Him.”
Not to you anymore.

You spent years building something. You obeyed when no one was watching. You stood in the wilderness when it was lonely. You spoke truth when it cost you reputation. You called sin what it was. You didn’t compromise.
And now… it feels like you’re being replaced.
That’s where he was.
John.
The one who prepared the way. The voice crying in the wilderness. The one who baptized crowds, confronted kings, and shook a generation awake.
And suddenly, the attention shifted to Jesus.
Not gradually.
Decisively.
His own disciples came to him, unsettled, almost defensive on his behalf:
“Rabbi, he who was with you across the Jordan, to whom you bore witness—look, he is baptizing, and all are going to him.” (John 3:26)
Read that again.
All are going to Him.
This is the moment most people fail.
Not in obscurity.
In transition.
When what God used you to build starts pointing away from you.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
John didn’t fight for recognition.
He released it.
“A person cannot receive even one thing unless it is given him from heaven.” (John 3:27)
God saw it.
The hidden temptation to hold on.
The subtle desire to stay important.
The quiet voice that says, “You deserve this.”
You knew.
John could have protected his platform. He could have adjusted his message. He could have found a way to stay central.
Instead, he said something that exposes every ego still alive in us:
“He must increase, but I must decrease.” (John 3:30)
Not “we must grow together.”
Not “I’ll support Him while maintaining my influence.”
Decrease.
That word doesn’t trend well.
It doesn’t build brands.
It kills self.
And that’s the point.
Because the Gospel was never about your recognition.
It was always about your surrender.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
Some of you are exhausted not because God left you…
…but because you’re trying to hold on to something He already reassigned.
You feel overlooked.
Forgotten.
Replaced.
But what if this isn’t rejection?
What if this is alignment?
John understood something most believers resist:
Your assignment is temporary.
Your obedience is eternal.
And your identity was never meant to be built on being seen.
“The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom’s voice.” (John 3:29)
Do you hear that?
He found joy… not in being the center…
…but in stepping aside when the Bridegroom arrived.
That’s a different kind of heart.
A heart that doesn’t need applause to stay faithful.
A heart that recognizes Jesus when He steps into the room—even if it means stepping out yourself.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because some of you say you follow Jesus…
…but panic when attention shifts away from you.
You serve… but secretly hope to be noticed.
You give… but expect acknowledgment.
You lead… but struggle when someone else rises.
God saw it.
And He’s not ignoring it.
He’s confronting it.
Because pride doesn’t always shout.
Sometimes it quietly resists decrease.
And that resistance reveals something deeper:
You’ve attached your worth to recognition.
But Scripture cuts through that illusion:
“For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? … If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ.” (Galatians 1:10)
There it is.
You can’t hold on to both.
Recognition or obedience.
Platform or surrender.
Self or Christ.
And here’s the truth most avoid:
You don’t lose anything by stepping back when God says step back.
You only lose the illusion that it was ever yours.
“Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory.” (Psalm 115:1)
Read that again.
Not to us.
John lived that.
And it cost him everything.
His following.
His influence.
Eventually… his freedom.
And still, he didn’t take it back.
Because when you’ve truly seen Jesus…
recognition becomes irrelevant.
Now look at your own life.
Where are you gripping too tightly?
Where are you quietly resisting decrease?
Where are you trying to remain visible when God is asking you to become faithful?
This is the moment.
Not public.
But real.
Where you decide who this is really about.
Jesus didn’t come to share glory.
He came to receive it.
And salvation only begins when self steps off the throne.
“For whoever would save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.” (Matthew 16:25)
Lose it.
Not manage it.
Not negotiate it.
Surrender it.
That’s where grace meets you.
Because you were never meant to carry the weight of being seen.
You were meant to reflect Him.
And here’s the invitation you’ve been avoiding:
Let go.
Not because you’re forgotten.
But because you’re being refined.
Not because you’re unimportant.
But because He is infinitely more.
If something in you is resisting this…
that’s the place He’s pointing at.
Say it if you feel it pressing on your chest:
“He must increase.”
Not halfway.
Not later.
Now.
Let it land. Let it confront you. Let it correct you.
There’s more of this depth waiting—truth that doesn’t flatter you but transforms you, Scripture that cuts and heals at the same time. That’s what you step into when you go deeper.
Follow this path, not for content—but for correction.
And if you felt that conviction… don’t hide it. Put it into words. Let it be real.
